- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after 2–3 consecutive positive sentiment days) — add a small upward bias to forecast peaks.  
- Model overestimates downward moves in low-sentiment periods — reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is consistently negative over last 5–7 days.  
- Forecast tends to lag true price by 1–3 days in high-sentiment periods — adjust forward 1–2 days if sentiment is trending up.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment is strong.  
- Overshoot after spikes (especially >10% from prior peak) — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment is neutral or cooling.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often underestimate late-period spikes — add 0.5–1.5% buffer if sentiment is rising in last 5 days.
